_comment: What the night queue actually did with each Issue, from the run of
2026-09-21. This is the ground truth the recordings beside it are scored
against: a gate verdict is a prediction, and this says whether it was right.
The outcome recorded here is whether a pull request implementing the Issue
exists, not what the queue reported. The two disagree: the queue called
#218 and #224 failures, and both produced a PR anyway. Scoring against the
queue's own report would have taught the gate to predict the runner's
bookkeeping rather than whether the work got done.
'cause' names why a failure happened, because only some failures are
knowable from an Issue at all. A dependency on unmerged work is visible in
the Issue text. The runner exhausting its 40-call tool budget is not — that
is a property of the executor, and a check that appears to predict it is
hexbound runs no CI on pull requests, so 'succeeded' means a PR implementing
the Issue was opened, not that it has been reviewed or merged.
run: night_issue 2026-09-21, sige31ymail/hexbound, 9 Issues, 6 produced a PR

218.evidence: PR #232, opened after the queue had already recorded worker_output_invalid: the parent task returned without its final JSON while the delegated child kept running and finished the work

219.evidence: no changes, no PR: the Master Passive foundation from #218 was not on main

220.evidence: no changes, no PR: needed #218 and #219, neither merged

222.evidence: cancelled at the 40-call tool limit mid-run; worktree preserved, no commit, no PR

224.evidence: PR #233, opened after the queue recorded a tool-limit cancellation: 901 tests and typecheck had already passed, and the cancellation landed during browser verification rather than during the implementation
